```plato

//==
// # ICurve capability interfaces
//
// The optional capabilities a curve may satisfy on top of the `ICurve<TRange>`
// root declared above: an explicit period, first and second
// derivatives, a moving frame, planarity, polar form, and arc-length
// parameterization. Split from the roots because a file holds at most twelve
// top-level declarations and because these are opt-in refinements rather than
// classifications. Bodies live in `curves.library.plato`.

// A curve whose parameterization repeats: evaluating at t and t + Period yields
// the same position. All closed curves may be traversed periodically; a periodic
// curve makes the period explicit. TRange is the evaluated value type (Number,
// Point2D, or Point3D); inheriting ICurve makes the wrapped evaluation
// Eval(t mod Period) derivable (see EvalWrapped in curves.library.plato)
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periodic_function).
interface IPeriodicCurve<TRange>
    inherits IPeriodic<Number>, ICurve<TRange>
{ }
```
